# Message Delivery Guarantees
> Verified against: .NET 9 | C# 13 | Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR 9.x
> Last reviewed: 2026-02-22

## The Law
Treat SignalR as at-most-once delivery — guarantee at-least-once delivery at the database layer, and make all message operations idempotent so duplicate delivery is harmless.

## Why This Kills You At Scale
A user sends a message. The server saves it, calls `NotifyMessageSentAsync`, the SignalR call throws due to a transient Redis backplane error. The developer catches the exception and retries — now the notification is sent twice. The client receives the same message twice and displays a duplicate. At 100k messages/day with a 0.1% transient failure rate, users see 100 duplicate messages per day. Alternatively: developer does not retry, messages are silently lost. Both outcomes are production bugs.

## The Pattern

```csharp
#nullable enable
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

// ✅ Correct: idempotent message creation — client generates ID, server deduplicates
public sealed class MessageService(
    IMessageRepository messageRepo,
    IUnitOfWork unitOfWork,
    IRealTimeNotifier notifier,
    ILogger<MessageService> logger)
{
    public async Task<MessageDto> SendAsync(
        SendMessageRequest request,
        CancellationToken ct)
    {
        // ✅ Client-generated ID — client can safely retry with same ID
        // If server received it first time, second attempt returns same message
        // No duplicate in DB, no duplicate in UI
        var existingMessage = await messageRepo.GetByIdAsync(request.ClientMessageId, ct);
        if (existingMessage is not null)
        {
            // Already processed — idempotent return
            logger.LogDebug("Duplicate message request {MessageId} — returning existing", request.ClientMessageId);
            return existingMessage.ToDto();
        }

        var message = new Message
        {
            Id = request.ClientMessageId, // Client owns the ID
            ConversationId = request.ConversationId,
            SenderId = request.SenderId,
            Content = request.Content,
            SentAt = DateTime.UtcNow,
            // ✅ Track delivery status
            DeliveryStatus = DeliveryStatus.Saved
        };

        await messageRepo.AddAsync(message, ct);
        await unitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync(ct);

        var dto = message.ToDto();

        // ✅ Notify after commit — at-most-once from SignalR's perspective
        // The DB is the guarantee — SignalR is best-effort delivery on top
        await notifier.NotifyMessageSentAsync(request.ConversationId, dto, ct);

        return dto;
    }
}

// ✅ Correct: delivery status tracking — for reliable UI feedback
public enum DeliveryStatus
{
    Saved,      // Persisted to DB — guaranteed not lost
    Delivered,  // Received by recipient's SignalR connection
    Read        // Recipient opened the conversation
}

// ✅ Correct: message DTO includes delivery status — UI shows checkmarks
public sealed record MessageDto(
    Guid Id,
    string Content,
    Guid SenderId,
    DateTime SentAt,
    DeliveryStatus Status);

// ✅ Correct: client sends ClientMessageId (UUID v4 generated client-side)
public sealed record SendMessageRequest(
    Guid ClientMessageId,  // UUID generated by Angular before sending
    Guid ConversationId,
    string Content,
    Guid SenderId);

// ✅ Correct: mark delivered when client receives via SignalR
[Authorize]
public sealed class ChatHub(IMessageService messageService) : Hub<IChatClient>
{
    // Client calls this to acknowledge receipt — server updates DeliveryStatus
    public async Task AcknowledgeDelivery(Guid messageId)
    {
        await messageService.MarkDeliveredAsync(
            messageId,
            Context.ConnectionAborted);
    }
}

// ✅ Correct: deduplicate at DB level with unique constraint
// In migration:
// migrationBuilder.CreateIndex(
//     name: "IX_Messages_ClientMessageId",
//     table: "Messages",
//     column: "Id",  // Primary key is the client-generated ID — unique by definition
//     unique: true);

// Handle the case where concurrent duplicate requests both pass the existence check:
public async Task<MessageDto> SendSafeAsync(SendMessageRequest request, CancellationToken ct)
{
    try
    {
        return await SendAsync(request, ct);
    }
    catch (DbUpdateException ex) when (IsDuplicateKeyException(ex))
    {
        // Race condition — two identical requests arrived simultaneously
        // Both passed the "does it exist?" check, one won the insert race
        // Return the winner's result
        var existing = await messageRepo.GetByIdAsync(request.ClientMessageId, ct)
            ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Message should exist after duplicate key exception");
        return existing.ToDto();
    }
}

private static bool IsDuplicateKeyException(DbUpdateException ex)
    => ex.InnerException?.Message.Contains("duplicate key", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) == true
    || ex.InnerException?.Message.Contains("UNIQUE constraint", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) == true;

// ❌ Wrong: server-generated ID + no idempotency — retries create duplicates
public async Task<MessageDto> SendInsecureAsync(string content, Guid conversationId, CancellationToken ct)
{
    var message = new Message
    {
        Id = Guid.NewGuid(), // New ID every call — retries = duplicates
        Content = content,
        ConversationId = conversationId
    };
    await messageRepo.AddAsync(message, ct);
    await unitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
    return message.ToDto();
}
```

## The Trap

```csharp
// A senior developer implements client-generated IDs and idempotency correctly.
// No duplicates. Ships.
// The trap: Angular generates UUID v4 correctly, but retries on network error
// include a DIFFERENT message ID each time — because the retry logic
// generates a new ID instead of reusing the original.

// Angular service (TypeScript — for reference):
// ❌ Wrong retry — new ID each attempt
sendMessage(content: string, conversationId: string): Observable<MessageDto> {
    return this.http.post<MessageDto>('/api/messages', {
        clientMessageId: crypto.randomUUID(), // New ID each call — retries create duplicates
        content,
        conversationId
    }).pipe(
        retry(3)
    );
}

// ✅ Correct retry — same ID each attempt
sendMessage(content: string, conversationId: string): Observable<MessageDto> {
    const clientMessageId = crypto.randomUUID(); // Generated ONCE before the request
    const request = { clientMessageId, content, conversationId };

    return this.http.post<MessageDto>('/api/messages', request).pipe(
        retry({ count: 3, delay: (error, retryCount) => timer(retryCount * 1000) })
        // Same `request` object used for all retries — same clientMessageId
    );
}

// The ID must be generated before the retry wrapper — not inside the observable factory.
// This is a JavaScript closure scoping issue that passes every code review
// because the retry() operator hides the re-subscription behavior.
```

## The Exception
Internal system-generated messages (automated notifications, system announcements, bot messages) are generated server-side with server-assigned IDs — they are not user-initiated and have no client to generate an idempotency key. These should have their own deduplication mechanism based on the triggering event ID (e.g., `notificationEventId`) rather than client-generated IDs.

## Before You Merge
- Does the message creation endpoint accept a client-generated `ClientMessageId` and return the existing message if it is already processed?
- Does the DB have a unique constraint on `Messages.Id` — preventing duplicate inserts at the storage level?
- Does the service catch `DbUpdateException` for duplicate key violations and return the existing record — not throw 500?
- Does the Angular retry logic generate the UUID once before the retry wrapper — not inside the observable?
- Is SignalR treated as best-effort delivery on top of DB persistence — never as the primary delivery guarantee?
